agenda_text:
CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
November 4, 2020 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 ((https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf)), please  note
that members of the public will only be allowed to observe and
address the Planning Commission Meeting of November 4, 2020 at
7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other electronic means, as
follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public
Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/
   The above access options provide the public with the
  opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.
   However, members of the public who wish to orally address the
  Planning Commission must use the public access options noted
  below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments:
Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 8181121##

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

    When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.
    If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35
  while also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you
  mute the sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds
  from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are
  making public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible
  due to feedback.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on November 4, 2020,
the day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting
date and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior
to close of the public hearing will be made part of the official
public record of the meeting.
[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on
Following Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda
  other than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  Minutes approval for February 5, 2020, Planning Commission
  meeting.

6.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2020-
  003(ZCA-2020-003)  to  modify  Self-Storage  Facility
  regulations citywide.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2020-096;and
  2) Adopt a resolution recommending City Council
  adoption of Zone Code Amendment 2020-003 (ZCA-2020-
  003).

7.  NON - PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Sandy
  Sigal, representing NewMark Merrill Companies, for Design
  Review No. 2020-006 (DR-2020-064) to allow a 936 square-
  foot mural on the exterior of a one-story commercial
  building that is part of an existing shopping center on an
  approximately 17-acre, C-2(General Commercial) zoned
  property at 2876 West Imperial Highway.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2020-103; and
  2) Adopt a resolution approving DR-2020-006 subject to
  conditions.

8.  Commission Initiatives.

9.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

10.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230, One
Manchester Boulevard, Fourth Floor,  Inglewood City Hall,
Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must
be received 48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s). "Si no
entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor de
llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of November 4,
2020 is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or
other agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-
public hearing agenda item will automatically be continued to the
next regular Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing  materials  are  available  at
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-
Commission-4 and at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk
during regular business hours. If any additional documents are
received for distribution to the Planning Commission after
publication of this Agenda but before 12:00 P.M. on the day of the
  2
 meeting, they will be made available for public inspection at the
following  webpage
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-
Commission-4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future
Commission meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission
agendas for public participation option procedures at that time.)

February 5, 2020 Minutes
   MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 2020

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, February 5, 2020 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:05 p.m.

Chairman Springs wanted to welcome the Planning Commissioners
newest Commissioner to this evenings meeting, Commissioner
Patricia Patrick.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Terry Coleman
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that staff has received two emails for Item 6A;
that there will be a Revised Resolution for Item 6A and will be
presented by staff to the Planning Commission and copies have been
distributed on the public table along with each of the Planning
Commissioners’ seats; and the next Planning Commission Meeting for
the month of March will have a change of date and will take place
at a later date in March.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Commissioner Trejo made the motion to approve the minutes of
September 4, 2019 and was seconded by Commissioner Coleman.

MOTION:

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, Coleman and Chairman Springs.

Chairman Springs asked if there is a motion to take some of the
public hearing items out of order, by hearing Item 6B before Item
6A.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020

MOTION:

Commissioner Trejo made the motion to approve taking the public
hearing items out of order, by hearing Item 6B before Item 6A and
was seconded by Commissioner Coleman.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners  Patrick,  Trejo,  Coleman  and  Chairman
  Springs.

Abstained: Commissioner Rice

Commissioner Rice recused himself from hearing Item 6B, due to
conflict of interest.

(6) PUBLIC HEARING:

6B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-001 (SP-2020-001) 207 SOUTH MARKET
STREET. A public hearing to consider an application by Betelehem
Woldegiorgis, representing Nile Restaurant & Bar, for Special Use
Permit No. 2020-001 (SP-2020-001) to allow 1) the on-site
consumption of beer and wine, and distilled spirits and 2) live-
entertainment within a proposed bar on an approximately 8,625
square-foot, H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 207 South Market
Street.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Mr. Jackson asked all Planning Commissioners to ensure they utilize
the microphones as the meeting is being transmitted to the overflow
area for the public in the Community Room on the first floor.

Commissioner Patrick stated she had only one question for staff –
 What about the parking for this business and are there any
  spaces in the back? Does this mean everyone else will have to
  park on the street or other locations?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that there are only two parking spaces in
  the rear.

Commissioner Trejo stated she had questions for staff –
 So the only difference between this Item from the one in
  November, which was approved with the requirement that the
  applicant must serve food, ABC has determined that this cannot
  be made a condition of approval from the City, is that correct,
  but the applicant can still serve food is that correct?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, that is correct.

Commissioner Coleman stated that he has a statement for staff-
 On page three of the Resolution’s conditions number five –
  states that “...Exterior cameras must provide surveillance but
  cameras must be capable of producing a retrievable image on film
  or tape that can be made into a permanent record...” well this
  is a new era and the year is 2020, where cameras are now digital
  and therefore this statement should be either modified or
  removed.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the planning commission and speak about her project.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020
Betelehem Woldegiorgis, the owner came forward to address and speak
regarding her project. Ms. Kesha Bristow, representing the
contractor on the project came to assist Ms. Woldegiorgis present
to the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the planning commission if they had any
questions for the applicant and her representative.

Commissioner Coleman asks the applicant -
 With regards to the parking for the staff employees and the lack
  of spaces near the restaurant, will the applicant attempt to
  connect with the other property owners to receive approval to
  park in their designated spaces after hours and through the
  evenings when their businesses are closed?
  - Ms. Woldegiorgis stated yes, she will.
  - Ms. Bristow stated that with regards to the parking, since
  the project is in the TOD site we are within our parking
  requirements.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments to speak
for or against this project.

 6. Salvador Arnold – DJ for Restaurant,  For Item 6B

 9. Eugene Goring  – Inglewood Resident/Patron,  For Item 6B

12. Mary Cochran  – Business Owner,  For Item 6B
13. Kesha Bristow  – Inglewood Resident/Patron,  For Item 6B

Chairman Springs closed the public speaking segment and called for
questions and final remarks from the planning commission.

Chairman Springs closed and thanked the Planning Commission for
their input, and asked for a motion regarding Special Use Permit
No. 2020-001 (SP-2020-001).

MOTION:

The motion was made by Commissioner Trejo to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-105 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2020-001 Special Use Permit SP-2020-001, subject to
16 conditions noted plus incorporating two additional conditions
for consideration in accordance are a requirement that the
applicant post no loitering signs on the outside of the building
exterior and a requirement that the applicant return to the
planning commission within one year before the planning
commission for review within one year within opening the new bar
and was seconded by Commissioner Coleman, that Resolution No.
1855;

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR
  BETELEHEM  WOLDEGIORGIS,  REPRESENTING  THE
  NILE, TO ALLOW THE ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF
  BEER, WINE, AND DISTILLED SPIRITS, AND LIVE-

  APPROXIMATELY  8,625  SQUARE-FOOT,  H-C
  (HISTORIC CORE) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 207

Be approved.

Chairman Springs asked for questions from the planning commission.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners  Patrick,  Trejo,  Coleman  and  Chairman
  Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-012 (SP-2019-012) AT 720 SOUTH
HINDRY AVENUE. A continued public hearing to consider an
application by Matt Budney, representing 7-Eleven, for Special Use
Permit No. 2019-010 (SP-2019-010) to allow 1) an automobile service
station and 2) the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption
from a proposed convenience market on an approximately 23,100
square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 1500-1502
North La Brea Avenue.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
 She stated that she believes she missed the part about the
  ingress and egress for the delivery trucks,
 Also what about the people, is there a set way or expected set
  way for the public to enter and exit when purchasing gasoline
  only or will it just be havoc?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant utilized a parking study
  and based on what the engineer observed that there is a lot
  of parking at the site between the hours of 4:00pm to 6:00pm,
  and the applicant is here and can speak to the peak hours
  along with how the interior of the facility activity that is
  occurring at that time and thus that analysis lead to the
  anticipated demand of the site based off of when the parking
  was being utilized the most.
 Regarding having security guards, is there only going to be one
  security guard at night and none during the daytime? And is
  this typical for most 7/11’s and or for other businesses in that
  area?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that is what is currently being proposed.
  - Ms. Fewell referred the Commissioner’s question to the
  applicant.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020

  She stated she wanted clarification of the Inglewood Municipal
  Code regarding the statement “...there shall be no dispensing
  or sale of gasoline or other motor fuels from the premises on
  which liquor sales are permitted...”, does that liquor mean
  everything other than beer and wine or when they use liquor in
  the IMC, does that include beer and wine – she stated she was
  not sure.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that it includes distilled spirits only.
  Most 7/11’s are either franchised or corporate owned, and she
  doesn’t remember seeing anything that spoke to the owner of this
  particular 7/11, who will the owner be?
  - Ms. Fewell referred this question to the applicant.

Commissioner Rice asked staff -
 He stated that he wanted to clarify why everyone is at the
  meeting this evening? And stated it appears that after not
  having to show a necessity and convenience for this project to
  be at this location, basically this body is here to approve the
  building of the service station and the beer and wine is that
  right?
 Actually, this action is under by-right and can be built
  regardless, correct?
  - Staff clarified that the convenience market w/o alcohol sales
  is by right.
 Also, was there an overall traffic study done for both foot and
  vehicle traffic into the 7/11?
  - Ms. Fewell stated there was no traffic study done for the
  pedestrian traffic, but a circulation study was done for the
  delivery trucks.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that Public Works typically also takes a
  look at the general circulation use by both individual and
  vehicle traffic needs, along with deliveries at the location
  in use and it was determined that there is no substantive
  change to traffic patterns.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Why was this continued so many times? Was it to address the
  concerns of the community by the applicant, because it went from
  September, until now, February. So then, I will ask this
  question of the applicant, because there were some of the
  concerns that needed to be addressed.
  - Ms. Fewell stated it was continued several times, due to the
  fact that the applicant wanted to meet several times with the
  community.
 On the security cameras will they pick up some or all of the
  activity that occurs in the alley-way? I know that what I see
  on the plans, there are two fish-eyed cameras on the gasoline
  canopies and then there is one at the north-east corner of 64th
  Street and the Alley-way. I just want to make sure that there
  will be some attention given to capturing the activities in the
  alley, will this be addressed during site plan review – do you
  know?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that there was a requirement given to have
  the applicant place the cameras high above the wall to ensure
  that the alley-way is captured at all times along with the
  public right-of-way.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020
Commissioner Coleman made a statement to staff -
 Security and safety are my main concerns. Feels that two fish-
  eyed cameras on top of the gasoline canopies, are not enough
  for complete coverage of the eight pumps, where identifying
  real-time video can be done to insure that no one tampers with
  the card readers for payment by the customers, along with
  covering the alley-way to defuse any illegal activity there,
  not to mention just covering the front doors of the 7/11, he
  personally feels that two cameras are not enough for the
  security and safety of this project.

Chairman Springs stated he had no questions at this time and opened
the floor for the applicant to come forward and speak about this
project and to express the benefits that this project will have
for the community and that it is something that the community
really wants in their neighborhood.

Mr. Arman Ross, Representative for 7/11 Stores and the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked Mr. Ross –
 Stated that even though Mr. Ross answered her earlier question
  as to who will be the owner of this particular store, she stated
  that it is her understanding that 7/11 has made a campaign to
  open more stores, and presently there are eleven 7/11 stores in
  the City of Inglewood, seven in Culver City, five in Hawthorne
  and seven in Gardena. She asked what is the present plan with
  opening more stores in those different cities and will it be as
  many as there presently are now in Inglewood, and if not why
  not?
  - Mr. Ross stated that 7/11 feels it best to open new stores in
  the demographics that would support the new stores. Like any
  other retailer, they look at the demographics in the
  surrounding area, if there is a lack of supermarkets, or lack
  of convenience stores and a lack of like businesses, that
  might be the place that 7/11 would want to build. The quality
  and economic investment that 7/11 puts into its stores,
  upwards of three million dollars’ worth of investment to build
  its stores, they believe and have seen this attract other
  high-end investors and like businesses to that particular
  area.

Commissioner Rice stated to the applicant –
 With this particular project being built in the district that
  he presently is a member of, there is one thing that will not
  be allowed or tolerated and that is not being true to the designs
  and plans that are outlined and shown today, and with that
  because of what this community stands for there will be the
  requirement of a one-year review before this Planning Commission
  and if there is anything that does not meet exactly what these
  plans are saying will be, then this project will cancelled.
  - Mr. Ross stated that for sure, everything that is outlined in
  the plans and stated to be built, will be. He also stated
  that he would be available for contact by anyone present this
  evening, even after the project is complete and the franchisee
  takes control, he will be available to make sure that all
  conditions are met.

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020

Commissioner Trejo stated to the applicant –
 When she drove past the site, she noticed how dark the area
  appeared to be and even though presently it is an abandoned
  area, and although there are several 7/11 stores throughout the
  City of Inglewood, she stated she feels that something of this
  nature, would be an improvement to the corner of 64th street
  and La Brea, and just as you have made promises and what seems
  to be a sincere commitment to Commissioner Rice and the people
  of this community, you will have to adhere to all conditions of
  approval.
 She would like a roving patrol set at no less than 24 to as long
  as 60 months which will be determined also in site plan review.
  This will help to insure that there will be no loitering in and
  around the area along with the alley-way being patrolled. Again
  with the one-year review, this is something that can be
  reexamined to see that what is set up is working and will help
  to alleviate any concerns with the local community.
  - Mr. Ross stated that would be fine and that he is willing to
  do whatever site plan review determines.

Commissioner Coleman stated to the applicant –
 His main concern is health and safety and he wanted to hear you
  say would you be willing to increase the number of security
  cameras to four?
 Next he wanted to hear that he would be willing to come back
  before the Planning Commission within one year for a
  reevaluation of the project and bring along with him the crime
  report from the Inglewood Police Department for submission to
  the Planning Commission?
  - Mr. Ross stated yes.
  - Again, Mr. Ross stated yes, he will do that.

Chairman Springs stated his question for the applicant –
 At one time, there was a Phillips 76 gas station at that corner
  and the question is are those tanks still there in the ground
  at that site?
  - Mr. Ross stated that there were two phases performed at the
  site, and with phase one, all tanks were proven to be removed
  from the ground and during phase two, the area has no
  residuals from the previous tanks, so the soil is clean.
 Prior to coming before the Planning Commission, he understood
  that there were several community forums conducted, and asked
  who was in attendance at those meetings?
  - Mr. Ross stated that yes, they did meet with the community
  and with him were his associate Mr. Michael Stewart and Mr.
  Jeff Williams from 7/11. He also stated his apologies that
  Mr. Williams could not attend the Planning Commission’s
  meeting as this particular evening there is an employee
  nationwide mandatory 7/11 meeting with all hands on deck and
  so he sends his apologies for not being here.

  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020

  As a result of that particular community forum, what was the
  outcome from the community? He stated that he needed to know
  what were the concerns of the community and what were the
  promises made to them from Mr. Ross and 7/11.
  - Mr. Ross stated that some of the concerns were what he
  addressed in his opening presentation to the Planning
  Commission this evening, the crime that might be drawn to the
  area and the environmental concerns regarding the gas
  station, whether or not the location of the present fault
  line, if it would be a factor there at the site, along with
  the environmental typo as it was labeled a class 2 categorical
  exemption and it should have been a class 3. There was a
  discussion if the soil had been cleaned properly. There was
  discussion and concern about traffic, traffic patterns and
  whether or not it will bring new people in the area. There
  was a concern about the traffic light there at 64th street
  and La Brea and there tends to be a heavy back-up of traffic
  on 64th street and though they let the community know that
  the street light was not an issue that belonged to 7/11, they
  would let the public works division know about the community’s
  concern about the traffic light. There was also a question
  about gas stations that are presently in the area and that
  was addressed with the fact that the owner of the property
  wishes to return the site to its previous fuel dispensing
  site. There was a concern about security and we stated that
  security will be administered at the site. And last, there
  was a question about ample parking on the site for both
  employees and patrons and we addressed that question, also
  there was a question to EV parking slots, but we feel that
  might not be a factor at this point.
  Well after that community forum, is it safe to say that the
  community was pleased with what you had to say to them and they
  left the meeting feeling happy about what can take place at the
  site?
  - Mr. Ross stated, well he wouldn’t say that the residents were
  pleased, he stated that he believed that a lot of the
  community came with a pre-disposed desire for the site and
  wanted to have a full sit-down restaurant, and stated that it
  was something that was not in 7/11’s control, as it was the
  site owners desire that they were fulfilling.

  He stated that as Commissioner Patrick has already pointed out
  that there are eleven 7/11 stores in Inglewood already and the
  fact that Mr. Ross did a fantastic presentation this evening in
  what 7/11 is desiring to bring to the site, he can see that the
  community is here this evening and the looks on their faces of
  frustration and dislike is very overwhelming. Chairman Springs
  then asked Mr. Ross if he was a resident of the City of
  Inglewood, and Mr. Ross stated no, and Chairman Springs said
  that he felt that Mr. Ross did not present what the community
  needs in his address on this evening, he presented what 7/11
  had to offer, but it does not appear to be what this community
  wants, and although his colleagues feel that 7/11 would be a
  nice change at that location, if there was not a service station
  being proposed at this site, would it be possible for 7/11 to
  operate without the service station?
  - Mr. Ross stated that once 7/11 crunched all of the numbers,
  with regards to the store with the service station, it is the
  wishes of the property owner to have this type of setup at
  the site and the beer and wine, although a small part of the
  sales at the site, in order for the project to be a success,
  all components would have be a factor.

  8
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 5, 2020

  Chairman Springs asked if Mr. Ross was aware that there is a
  convenience store on the SE side of the street and even though
  they will not have fresh fruits such as 7/11, they also have a
  car-wash.
  - Mr. Ross stated that if those customers want to stay with
  that store, it is alright, because there will be customers
  that will stop in at the 7/11 that will not go back to that
  particular convenience store, which are items that are only
  being provided at 7/11. If there is a game on, while there is
  half time, a quick run to the 7/11, grab some fruit, some
  sandwiches, a pack of beer, water, sweets, all from the 7/11
  and then back to the home. This is the convenience that will
  be provided to the community that is not presently there.

Chairman Springs stated to the applicant –
 What Mr. Ross is attempting to bring into the community is truly
  not the only convenience store in the area that will service
  the community and even though his colleagues feel that imposing
  a one year review, with added cameras and patrols for 2 to 4
  years is not what the community is asking for, as the planning
  commission received from one gentleman alone a small packet –
  that was thick with comments from the community stating that
  they do not wish to have this type of project in their community
  and so as Chairman, he is going to open the floor for the public
  to speak and verbally allow all to hear what is exactly on their
  minds.

Commissioner Coleman asked the applicant one more question –
 Will the security guards be armed or unarmed?
  - Mr. Ross stated that they will be unarmed, especially in a
  lower crime district such as this one.
